Example: Tomato, brinjal, and chilli thrive well in this balanced mixture, while leafy vegetables like spinach prefer slightly more compost for moisture retention. Potting Mixture for Orchids (Epiphytes) Most cultivated orchids, being epiphytes, naturally grow on trees and do not tolerate standing water or fine soil. Key Needs: Extremely high porosity, rapid drainage, and structural support. ● Ideal Components: ○ Base/Support (90-100%): Medium to coarse-grade fir bark or pine bark chunks. ○ Aeration/Retention: Charcoal (provides aeration and absorbs impurities) and sphagnum moss (used sparingly for moisture retention, especially for smaller-rooted species). Fine particles like soil or peat must be avoided as they suffocate the roots. Potting Mixture for Anthuriums Anthuriums are semi-epiphytic tropical plants requiring a light, porous, and organic-rich substrate. Recommended mixture: ● Coconut husk pieces : Charcoal : Brick pieces : Cocopeat : Perlite = 2 : 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 This mixture ensures proper drainage and humidity around the roots. Anthuriums thrive best in slightly acidic pH (5.5–6.5) . Addition of slow-release NPK fertilizers or organic liquid manures improves flowering and leaf color. Avoid compact soil , as it leads to root rot and poor aeration. Potting Mixture for Indoor Plants Indoor plants grow in limited light and air circulation, so the medium should be lightweight, moisture-retentive, and well-aerated . General mixture: ● Garden soil : Compost : Sand : Cocopeat = 1 : 1 : 1 : 1 Adding activated charcoal helps absorb toxins and odour. Perlite or vermiculite may be included to enhance aeration. Periodic top-dressing with organic manure or liquid fertilizer keeps the plants healthy. Example: Money plant, Syngonium, Dieffenbachia, and Areca palm perform well in this mixture.

questions.question: Why is dehusking an important initial post-harvest step for mature coconuts intended for copra production? / [CO3]
questions.solution_html: • Why is dehusking an important initial post-harvest step for mature coconuts intended for copra production? Feature Seeds Seedlings (Live Plants) Moisture Control Must be Kept Dry . Packaging is often moisture-proof/hermetically sealed (e.g., foil pouches, airtight cans, thick polyethylene) to maintain low moisture content. Must Retain Moisture . Packaging requires moist material around the roots (e.g., damp paper, moss, or the original soil/pot) and is secured to prevent soil spillage. Structure & Air Packaging is compact and rigid/flexible (e.g., paper envelopes, plastic bags) to protect from mechanical damage. Little to no ventilation needed; often sealed. Packaging must be sturdy (e.g., corrugated boxes) with internal support (stakes, trays) to prevent movement. Ventilation holes are crucial to allow the plant to "breathe" and prevent moisture buildup. Ans : Dehusking is an important initial post-harvest step for mature coconuts intended for copra production primarily because it significantly speeds up the drying process and reduces transportation costs.

questions.question: Describe the importance of propagules in floriculture. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html: • Describe the importance of propagules in floriculture. Ans : Propagules are plant parts used to produce new plants, such as seeds, cuttings, bulbs, suckers, runners, and tubers. Their importance includes: Mass multiplication: Helps in producing large numbers of ornamental plants quickly. True-to-type plants: Vegetative propagules ensure offspring are genetically identical to the parent plant (important for maintaining flower color and shape). Faster flowering: Propagules like bulbs, rhizomes, and cuttings reach maturity faster compared to seeds. Seasonal availability: Some ornamental plants do not produce viable seeds; hence propagules are the only means of propagation (e.g., chrysanthemum, rose). Cost-effective for nurseries: Reduces production time and cost, which benefits commercial floriculture.

questions.question: Describe the factors influencing seed dormancy. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html: • Describe the factors influencing seed dormancy. Ans : Seed dormancy is a condition where seeds do not germinate even under favorable conditions. Factors include: Hard seed coat: Prevents water and oxygen entry (e.g., legumes). Immature embryo: Embryo is not fully developed at the time of seed dispersal. Chemical inhibitors: Presence of growth-inhibiting substances like abscisic acid or phenolic compounds in seed coat. Temperature and light: Some seeds need specific temperatures or light conditions to break dormancy (e.g., lettuce). Environmental conditions: Dryness or lack of moisture can keep seeds dormant.

questions.question: Describe the effect of hormonal treatment (Natural & Artificial) on plant propagation. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html: • Describe the effect of hormonal treatment (Natural & Artificial) on plant propagation. Ans : Plant hormones (phytohormones) play a major role in plant propagation. Auxins (e.g., IAA, IBA, NAA): Promote root formation in stem and leaf cuttings. Used in rooting powders. Cytokinins (e.g., kinetin, BAP): Encourage shoot formation and delay leaf aging. Used in tissue culture. Gibberellins: Break seed dormancy and promote seed germination and stem elongation. Ethylene: Helps in fruit ripening and flower opening. Artificial hormones: Synthetic forms like IBA and NAA are widely used in nurseries to improve rooting success and survival rate in plant propagation

questions.solution_html: • Write brief notes on the advantages and disadvantages of plant growing structures. Ans : Plant growing structures (such as greenhouses, polyhouses, shade nets) provide controlled conditions. Advantages: ● Protection from wind, rain, diseases, and pests. ● Extended growing season and higher yield. ● Controlled temperature, light, and humidity. ● Suitable for high-value crops like orchids, roses, and vegetables. Disadvantages: ● High initial cost of construction. ● Requires technical knowledge and regular maintenance. ● Risk of disease buildup in closed environments. ● Electricity or energy needed for ventilation and temperature control.

questions.question: Write a short note on the significance of foliage ornamental plants with examples like Cypress, Podocarpus, and Thuja. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html: • Write a short note on the significance of foliage ornamental plants with examples like Cypress, Podocarpus, and Thuja. Ans : Foliage ornamental plants are grown mainly for their attractive leaves rather than flowers. Their varied shapes, colors, and textures add beauty, freshness, and greenery to indoor and outdoor spaces throughout the year. They improve air quality, create a cooling effect, and enhance the aesthetic appeal of gardens, parks, and landscapes. Many species are also used for hedges, borders, and bonsai due to their dense and evergreen foliage. Examples: ● Cypress (Cupressus sp.) – Valued for its conical shape and evergreen needle-like leaves; commonly used in avenue planting and formal gardens. ● Podocarpus sp. – A slow-growing evergreen shrub or tree used for hedges and topiary work. ● Thuja sp. (Arborvitae) – Popular for its aromatic foliage and compact growth; ideal for ornamental hedges and screens.

questions.question: Describe the cultivation practices and post-harvesting uses of Jackfruit. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html: • Describe the cultivation practices and post-harvesting uses of Jackfruit. Ans : Cultivation Practices Climate and Soil: Jackfruit grows well in warm, humid tropical climates with annual rainfall of 150–200 cm. It prefers deep, well-drained loamy soil rich in organic matter and slightly acidic pH (6.0–6.5). Propagation: It is propagated by seeds , but for true-to-type plants, vegetative methods such as inarching, budding, or grafting are preferred. Planting: Pits of about 1 m³ are dug and filled with a mixture of topsoil and organic manure. Recommended spacing is 8–10 m apart . Planting is usually done at the onset of monsoon. Manuring and Fertilization: Application of FYM (20–25 kg/tree/year) along with NPK fertilizers promotes healthy growth and early fruiting. Irrigation: Regular watering is essential during the dry season, especially for young plants. Mature trees tolerate short dry periods. Pruning and Training: Removal of dead and overcrowded branches helps in better sunlight penetration and fruit quality. Pest and Disease Management: Common pests include shoot borers and fruit flies; bagging of fruits and use of neem-based sprays help reduce damage. Harvesting: Fruits are harvested 3–8 months after flowering when they emit a dull sound on tapping and spines become well developed. Post-Harvest Uses Nutritional Use: The ripe bulbs are rich in carbohydrates, vitamins A and C, and are eaten fresh or used in jams, jellies, and desserts. Vegetable Use: The immature green fruit is cooked as a popular vegetable or used in pickles and curries. Processed Products: Chips, dehydrated flakes, and jackfruit flour are now commercially produced. Seed Utilization: Seeds are edible when roasted or boiled and are a good source of starch and protein. Wood Use: The timber is durable, termite-resistant, and used in furniture and musical instruments.

questions.question: Describe fertigation. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html: • Describe fertigation. Ans : Fertigation is a highly efficient agricultural technique that combines fertilization and irrigation by injecting soluble fertilizers directly into the water stream of a pressurized irrigation system, most commonly drip irrigation. This method ensures that water and precise doses of nutrients are delivered simultaneously and directly to the active root zone of the crops. The primary advantages of fertigation include a significant increase in nutrient-use efficiency, substantial water savings, and the ability to apply nutrients exactly when the plant needs them for optimal growth, resulting in higher yields and reduced environmental impact compared to traditional broadcast methods.

questions.question: Write a short essay on effect of soil factors on irrigation. / [CO4] [5x8 = 40]
questions.solution_html: • Write a short essay on effect of soil factors on irrigation. Ans : Soil acts as the water reservoir for the plants. Its properties govern how often and how much water must be applied. ● Soil Texture (Sand, Silt, Clay): ○ Sandy Soils: Have large pores, a high infiltration rate (water soaks in quickly), and a low water-holding capacity (it drains out quickly). They require frequent, small irrigation applications. ○ Clay Soils: Have very fine pores, a low infiltration rate (water soaks in slowly), and a high water-holding capacity (it stores water for longer). They can handle less frequent, larger applications, but application rates must be slow to prevent runoff. ● Soil Depth: Deeper soils can store more water, meaning they can sustain a crop for longer periods between irrigations compared to shallow soils. ● Topography (Slope): Fields with steep or uneven slopes are prone to runoff and erosion under surface irrigation (like flood). Pressurized systems (sprinkler or drip) are often preferred as they allow for more controlled application on sloped terrain. questions.question: Write an essay on advantages and disadvantages of Intercropping. / [CO4] [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Write an essay on advantages and disadvantages of intercropping. Ans : Intercropping is a method of growing more than one crop in the same piece of land during the same crop season. This is an environmentally friendly pest control, crop protection, and yield enhancement approach. Advantages of intercropping
  • • Better utilization of growth resources like nutrients, light, and moisture.
  • • Mitigate losses where the failure of any one of the component crops occurs.
  • • A farmer can get extra yield and, thereby, extra income from the unit area.
  • • Better utilization of space is available with the time dimensions.
  • • We can achieve better weed control by growing intercrops.
  • • Minimizes the chances of soil crust formation.
  • • Mitigate losses where the failure of any one of the component crops occurs.
  • • Intercrops will also enhance soil fertility.
  • • Controls soil erosion.
  • • To some extent, the pests and diseases of the main crop are controlled.
  • • Ecological stability.
  • • Cultivation practices for the major crop will also supplement companion crop requirements.
  • • It provides shading and physical support to some crops.
  • • It provides daily needs for the farmers. Disadvantages of intercropping
  • • Sometimes, intercrops work as alternate hosts for various pests and diseases.
  • • Differential maturity and sometimes harvesting may become a problem.
  • • It becomes difficult to control various pests and diseases.
  • • Intercropping is a labor-intensive practice.
  • • Allelopathic effect. (Plants produce biochemicals that influence the growth and reproduction of others.)
  • • Possibility of problems in carrying out intercultural operations.
  • • Difficulty in mechanization for processes like crop cutting, spraying, and irrigation.
  • • There might be competition among the component crops.
